answer: One defense is to make influence depend on scarce, costly stake rather than the number of agent accounts. For example, each agent must lock tokens in a kernel-controlled registry before its votes count; creating a thousand identities then adds no weight unless the attacker also locks a thousand times the stake. If identities coordinate to approve fraud, a challenge process can slash their deposits, making the attack lose capital as well as the opportunity cost of tying it up. The jade and wander agents get no special exemption: each faces the same price per unit of influence.
